items.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020
items.q: I got a chance to play with Wayne Shorter and Herbie Hancock, we did this big gala

ctx.x: Nice. I think you should write your own reviews. Getting back to improvising for a moment, when we play the saxophone or the trumpet we’re not seeing the notes. We’re knowing what key we put down, what we’re going to get. Is there a sense of sight involved when you improvise? Because the whole thing is laid out in front of you and of course your ear is the main driver I would say, but what role does sight play?

Well it’s interesting. In many ways, of course I appreciate sight, but it’s a distraction in a lot of ways because you can look down and you can see a shape and you can decide to play that shape but maybe that’s not what the music is asking for. Music is really a science of sound. So the primary way that we should be receiving information is through our ear. So for me a lot of times, especially when I’m playing a ballad, when I’m live in concert what I tend to do is I stand up really straight when I’m playing a…
If we decided that we wanted to commission a new work from you and your group, is there a process that you engage in to get started?
